title: The Checklist Before the Run: Ten Checks as Code, the Ones That Block and the Ones That Warn, and a Number That Is Not a Number

questions.question: What is the difference between a block and a warning?
options: A block is for hardware and a warning for software
A warning is checked first and a block last
A block can be overridden with a reason, a warning with none
A block stops the run; a warning may be overridden with a reason
questions.explanation: Which checks are blocks is a decision made beforehand. Six of the ten here stop the vehicle outright, and four leave the choice to a person who has to say why.

questions.question: Making each check fail alone blocked the run how many times?
options: 10: every failed check blocks
1: only the energy check blocks
questions.explanation: Energy, emergency stop, position, scan, geofence and release are blocks. Link, log space, clock and motor temperature are warnings, which is the other four.

questions.question: A state in which every number was not a number failed how many checks?
options: 10, every check
0: a comparison with it is always true
6, the blocks only
questions.explanation: Eight of the ten checks read a number. The geofence and the release are not numbers, so they were unaffected.

questions.question: With 5.00 Wh left, 4.50 needed and a reserve of 0.50, the energy check:
options: Failed; 5.01 would pass
Warned, and a person overrode it
Passed; 4.99 failed
Passed, as did 4.99
questions.explanation: 5.00 is exactly 4.50 plus 0.50, and the check is at least, not more than. The test is made at the edge, where the two differ.

questions.question: Why is every check written as 'ok when within the limit'?
options: It reads more naturally
It is faster to evaluate
A comparison with a number that is not a number is false, so it fails
So that a block and a warning look alike
questions.explanation: Any comparison with a value that is not a number is false. Written as ok when within the limit, a failed sensor fails the check; written the other way it would pass.

questions.question: What happens to an override of a block?
options: It is refused and reported
It is accepted if a reason is given
It turns the block into a warning
It is ignored and the run goes ahead
questions.explanation: Blocks cannot be argued with. The attempt is kept in the report as refused, so it can be seen that someone tried.
